title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This sheet is scratch paper on the back of a typescript page of SGA 7 exposé IX (the semi-stable reduction section, typed p. 34, between pp. 33 and 35). It holds two unrelated groups of jottings.

(1) Right-side-up, top half. Here S is a coalgebra over a field k, apparently the coordinate Hopf algebra of an affine group scheme. 'SL' and 'MON' suggest Grothendieck has in mind SL and the monoidal structure on representations. C is an S-comodule, i.e. a representation. ⊠_S is the cotensor product, defined as the equalizer of C⊗D ⇉ C⊗S⊗D. The structure equalizer is written explicitly as C → C⊗_k S ⇉ C⊗_k S⊗_k S. Here u_S denotes the comultiplication and u_C the coaction.

The notes record three basic facts and one question:
- S ⊠_S S = S.
- S ⊠_S C ≅ C.
- The boxed question: (M⊗_k S) ⊠_S C ≅ M⊗_k C ?, i.e. cotensoring a cofree comodule M⊗S with C gives M⊗C. This is proved by exhibiting M⊗C → (M⊗S)⊗C as the equalizer of id_M⊗u_S⊗id_C and id_M⊗id_S⊗u_C.
- The first lines compare M⊗S⊗M'⊗S with M⊗M'⊗S⊗S via the analogous maps. This checks compatibility of the tensor (monoidal) structure on comodules with cofree comodules.

Grothendieck then passes to the functor-of-points picture. V(N) denotes the vector-bundle-type functor with V(N)(h) = Hom_k(N, h) for k-algebras h. He writes V(M⊗_k S)(h') = Hom_{h'}(M⊗S⊗h', h') = Hom_k(M, S^{h'}), remarking that this is an S^{h'}-module. He also writes the action Hom_k(M, S^{h'}) × C^{h'} → C'^{h'}, which translates the coaction into an action of points. A first attempt, V(S)⊗V(C) → V(C'), is struck out.

This all looks like preliminary bookkeeping for a comodule or Hopf-algebra description of the objects in the divided-power de Rham lecture: PD-envelopes, the diagonal, and stratifications seen as comodules over a Hopf algebroid.

(2) Upside-down, largely struck through by a long diagonal line. It contains:
- a Hopf algebra 𝒜 with comultiplication 𝒜 → 𝒜⊗𝒜;
- a basis y_i with the remark 'Δ y_i = Σ y_j⊗y_k fini !', i.e. finiteness of the coproduct;
- a universal or canonical element ξ(M) = Σ t_i y_i, possibly '= cor(𝒜)', pairing a dual basis t_i with the y_i;
- symbols 𝒜^*(Σ,Σ',t), 𝒜^*(S,S',t), 𝒜^*(Σ'',Σ'',t''), apparently a family of algebras indexed by pairs of objects and a parameter, with composition between them;
- a chain Σ_k ← Σ_{k+1} ← …;
- {{T}}{{λ,−λ}}.

The fragments are too partial to reconstruct reliably. They resemble the formalism of a Hopf algebroid or algebra of operations with a canonical 'total' element. That is standard in the theory of formal groups and divided powers, e.g. the dual of the PD-polynomial algebra.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. The boxed isomorphism (M⊗S) □_S C ≅ M⊗C is correct: cofree comodules are cotensor-cofree, by the standard equalizer argument.
The upside-down part is crossed out and fragmentary, so its correctness cannot be assessed.

ideas.what: Cotensor product of comodules over a coalgebra or Hopf algebra S, with S□S = S, S□C = C, and (M⊗S)□_S C ≅ M⊗C
ideas.where_published: Comodules appear in SGA 3 (representations of affine group schemes as comodules); the cotensor formalism is not prominent there

ideas.what: Translating comodule structure into functor-of-points actions: Hom_k(M, S^{h'}) × C^{h'} → C'^{h'}
ideas.modern_name: Representations of affine group schemes via functor of points / comodule–representation equivalence

ideas.what: Hopf algebra 𝒜 with basis y_i having finite coproducts, and a canonical element Σ t_i y_i
ideas.modern_name: Canonical (universal) element of a Hopf algebra and its dual; algebra of operations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Milnor's dual Steenrod algebra, formal group theory)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine scratch computations about cotensor products of comodules and cofree comodules, plus a struck-out, fragmentary Hopf-algebra sketch. All of it is standard, and nothing on the page suggests a new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The right-hand column at the top most likely reads id_M⊗id_{M'}⊗u_S⊗id_S and id_M⊗id_{M'}⊗id_S⊗u_S, i.e. the maps on M⊗M'⊗S⊗S. The 'M' subscript is partly hidden.
'si [?] un S^h-module [?] !' should probably read 'est un S^{h'}-module !' (the image is unclear).
The braces in '{M⊗_k S}⊗_k C' are just Grothendieck's grouping. The overline marks the factor S⊗C on which the equalizer pair acts.
The upside-down 'Σ_k ← Σ_{k+}' is probably Σ_k ← Σ_{k+1}.
The upside-down part also contains a crossed-out 'idéal' or 'idéaux' near the top right, which the transcription omits.
